messages.content: The dates are settled now: Friday, October 10 through Tuesday, October 14, and our Capitol tour is Monday morning. I need a real comparison of the Penn Quarter and Dupont hotels before the rates move.
I can do that. What are the live rate details for each room, including taxes or required fees, and does each listing explicitly accept two adults and your 14-year-old?

Penn Quarter is $289 a night for two double beds. It adds a $35 nightly destination charge. Dupont is $329 a night for two queen beds with no destination fee. Washington hotel tax is 15.95%. Both show all four nights available, but I want you to check the occupancy issue carefully.

Using those figures, Penn Quarter is $1,156 in room charges plus $140 in destination charges, or $1,296 before tax. If the 15.95% tax applies to both the room and mandatory charge, the four-night total is $1,502.71. Dupont is $1,316 before tax and $1,525.90 after tax. That makes Dupont only $23.19 more overall, subject to confirming how the Penn fee is taxed.

That is much closer than the nightly prices made it look. The Penn listing says maximum occupancy four, and it let me enter two adults and one child age 14. Dupont says the same, but its room description calls the balcony room suitable for up to four guests.

Then both appear valid for three guests on paper. Penn provides two double beds; Dupont provides two queens, and the exact Dupont listing also identifies a balcony. Before payment, the final booking screen should still name all three guests or show occupancy for three, retain the selected bed type, and display every mandatory charge.

Yes. For a family trip where we will actually have downtime at the hotel, I would prioritize the room with a balcony when it is available. It is not an absolute requirement, but here the price gap is small enough to matter.

That gives Dupont a meaningful room advantage: larger beds and the balcony for about $5.80 more per night after tax. Penn still has the stronger sightseeing location. It is convenient for the National Mall, Air and Space, and the Capitol, while Dupont generally adds a Metro ride or a longer walk to those stops.
Put numbers around Monday morning. Our Capitol tour check-in is 8:20 a.m., and I do not want the location comparison left vague.

From Penn Quarter, allow roughly 20 to 30 minutes by Metro plus walking, or about 25 to 35 minutes on foot depending on the exact property. From Dupont Circle, allow roughly 30 to 40 minutes by Metro and walking. For an 8:20 a.m. check-in, I would plan to leave Penn around 7:40 and Dupont around 7:30, with extra margin if there is weekend-style service or an elevator outage. Exact times should be checked against the two hotel addresses and that morning's transit schedule.
Most of Saturday and Sunday will be Mall museums, but Friday evening and Tuesday morning are open. Does Dupont create enough inconvenience that Penn should still win?

Not enough to outweigh the room difference at these totals. Penn would save some transit time on the museum days and make Monday simpler, but the total savings are only $23.19. Dupont gives three people wider beds, a balcony for hotel downtime, and a neighborhood with useful options for the open periods. The additional travel is manageable if everyone is comfortable leaving about ten minutes earlier Monday.
Then identify the stronger choice, but be precise about what is verified versus what still needs checking. Do not book it.

The stronger choice is the Dupont Circle two-queen balcony room for October 10-14. Based on the figures provided, its estimated all-in four-night total is $1,525.90, only $23.19 above Penn Quarter's estimated $1,502.71. The listing currently indicates availability for all four nights, maximum occupancy of four, and suitability for two adults and one 14-year-old. Before reserving, verify the final taxed total, that no mandatory fee appears at checkout, that the exact two-queen balcony room remains assigned for three guests, and the cancellation deadline and penalty. Also confirm Monday morning transit from the exact address. Nothing has been booked.
